articles.summary: A Kuwaiti court has sentenced three individuals to death and eight others to five years in prison in a case involving an alleged plot to assassinate Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef and accusations of collusion with Iran and the Lebanese group Hezbollah. The verdict was issued by Kuwait’s State Security and Terrorism Crimes Court, presided over by Judge Nasser Al-Bader, alongside judges Omar Al-Mulaifi, Abdullah Al-Faleh and Salem Al-Zayed. According to the prosecution, the defendants faced charges of collaborating with foreign entities, planning hostile acts against Kuwait, targeting senior government officials, joining a banned organization and engaging in activities deemed harmful to national interests. The charges also included plans to use explosives in the assassination attempt and create panic among […]

articles.title: Election committee says no evidence of ballot tampering despite complaints from at least six parties
articles.summary:
Election committee says no evidence of ballot tampering despite complaints from at least six parties

Israel's Central Elections Committee (CEC) has said there is no evidence of systemic tampering with ballots in the election, despite complaints from at least six opposition parties.

The Times of Israel said that Yashar, B’Yachad, People of Israel, Yisrael Beytenu, Ra’am, and the Reservists-Economic party had all reported alleged irregularities, including "missing or defaced ballot slips and other suspected attempts to interfere with voting."

Yashar said they had raised a complaint after suspicions that reports of irregularities were not "isolated mishaps."

“The large number of incidents raises serious suspicions that these are not isolated mishaps, but rather a systematic and deliberate attempt to sabotage the democratic process, prevent citizens from exercising their right to vote and influence the election results,” they said in a statement.

articles.title: Palestinians are voting in Israel to ensure their very survival
articles.summary:
Palestinians are voting in Israel to ensure their very survival

Ibrahim Said has boycotted Israeli elections since voting in 1980.

Parties came and went, telling him they would defend his interests if elected, even promising to help return his lands in al-Birwa, the town his family were displaced from during the 1948 Nakba.

But nothing ever changed for the better for Palestinian citizens of Israel. Israeli democracy had nothing to offer him and his community, the 70-year-old felt.

This year, the situation is completely different.

“Without a doubt, we must vote this time. We are living in fear,” Said tells Middle East Eye in his garage in the Galilee.

Read more: Palestinians are voting in Israel to ensure their very survival

Jordánsko mezitím provedlo ozbrojený úder v Sýrii v reakci na předchozí incident, zatímco v Kuvajtu proběhly přísné rozsudky kvůli napojení na Írán a Hezbollah.
archive.security_status_en: Israel is holding pivotal parliamentary elections accompanied by high voter turnout and friction in the West Bank and around polling stations. Meanwhile, Jordan carried out a deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for a prior incident, and Kuwait handed down severe sentences over Iran-Hezbollah links.
archive.forecast_cs: V následujících dnech se očekává postupné sčítání hlasů a vyhodnocení výsledků izraelských voleb, které mohou výrazně ovlivnit směřování země. Lze také sledovat diplomatické dozvuky a reakce na přeshraniční aktivity v Sýrii a Kuvajtu.
archive.forecast_en: The coming days will see the gradual vote counting and evaluation of the Israeli election results, which could significantly steer the country's trajectory. Diplomatic reverberations and reactions to cross-border activities in Syria and Kuwait are also expected.
